about: Generalization benchmark G26 (train), in dev.json format. Tier 4 = a real product: bought-in parts (here a tube and countersunk screws) placed from a parts catalogue, holes and countersinks (subtraction), and fit, snap-deflection, mounting and printability requirements judged as interference and clearance checks against reference models. L1 ids match benchmarks/generalize/designs/G26/requirements.md, which holds the L2/L3 tree, the reference models, the assumptions and the traceability. Numbers that are not in the owner's words (clearance, strain limit, flange thickness, size limit) come from requirements.md sections 3 and 3.1 and are provisional. Never put any of these numbers in agent logic: they belong in the request text and in the parts' part.json.

methods.inspection: read from the design or mesh (counts, sizes, positions, relations)
methods.analysis: computed by Python (connectivity, interference and clearance against reference models, hand calculations, beam strain)
methods.demonstration: a stand-in object is placed in the design (fits, rests, does not slide)
methods.test: a probe is applied (push the tube in along the mouth direction, insert a screw along its axis)

requests.title: Snap tube clip for 12 mm rod
requests.request: A C-shaped snap clip for a 12 mm round tube (a solid rod or a pipe, 12 mm outside diameter). The clip mounts to a wall with two M3 countersunk screws 30 mm apart, side by side across the clip. The mouth opening is 10.5 mm, so the tube pushes in sideways and snaps into place; the arm thickness is 2.2 mm. The clip is 12 to 30 mm wide along the tube and is a single FDM printed part. Print it with the open side up, so that the layer lines run along the direction the arms flex.

l1.text: The design shall place the 12 mm tube from the parts catalogue seated in the clip's round bore, with the mouth facing up, and the two M3 countersunk screws in the wall holes, without the parts colliding, and shall declare that layout.

The clip shall hold the 12 mm tube in a round bore with a small clearance all round (0.05 to 0.15 mm per side) and wrap more than half of the tube, so that, across its axis, the tube can leave only through the mouth.

The mouth opening shall be 10.5 mm, and the tube shall push in through it along the mouth direction, touching the clip only at the two lips while it passes, with a lead-in that guides it (the lips' end faces sloping 20 to 60 degrees from horizontal).

The two arms shall be 2.2 mm thick, long enough to open by the 0.75 mm per side that the tube needs without exceeding 3 % bending strain (also with the worst-case tolerances: a 12.1 mm tube and a mouth 0.1 mm smaller, within 3.5 %), and free to flex.

The clip shall mount to a wall by two M3 countersunk screws exactly 30 mm apart, through countersunk holes that leave each screw head at or below the clip's surface and keep at least 1.5 mm of material around every hole on a flange 3 to 4 mm thick.
The clip's wall face shall be flat, with nothing protruding below it, and every screw shall be reachable with a screwdriver with the tube in place.
The clip shall print with its mouth up and its wall face on the bed, as one manifold body without supports, with the arms flexing in the plane of the layers.
The clip shall be no larger than 50 x 30 x 20 mm.
The design shall be delivered as the clip STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout and the agent's own clearance report, and that report shall agree with an independent measurement.
